source: Technology Promotion Project to Increase Productivity Around Tonle Sap (TSTD — TA 7305-CAM), watermelon (ដំណាំឪឡឹក) technical training booklet, prepared by the project's agricultural techniques and extension officer in cooperation with East West Seed International, November 2016. Contact: livleanghy@gmail.com
text:
Vine training (pruning/topping) of watermelon is done once the plant has developed about 5 true leaves/nodes on the main vine. At that point the growing tip is pinched back at around the 5th to 6th leaf so that the plant branches out into several side vines.

The booklet describes selecting and keeping a set number of the resulting side vines (around 5 vines mentioned in the source, or a reduced set of the 2 strongest vines depending on the grower's system) spread evenly across the bed, while removing weaker or excess shoots. Farmers are advised to keep the main productive vines to roughly 12 leaves/nodes, and to pinch off new growth beyond about the 13th node so plant energy goes into fruit development rather than continued vegetative growth.

Note: some of the specific numeric details in this section of the source were harder to read clearly due to font/scan quality; the general practice of early topping followed by selecting a limited number of strong side vines is clear, but the exact vine-count and node-count figures should be confirmed with a local agronomist or a clearer copy of the source before being treated as an exact recommendation.
